newsitem.title: DUBAI: More than 1,000 people have AIDS in Iran - minister.
newsitem.headline: More than 1,000 people have AIDS in Iran - minister.

text.p: More than 1,000 people in Iran suffer from AIDS and most of them contracted the disease through sexual contact, Iran's Health Minister Alireza Marandi said on Monday.

"The total number of people who have got AIDS in Iran stands at 1,047, with 70 to 80 percent of them contracting the deadly disease through sexual contacts," Marandi said in comments carried by the official Iranian news agency IRNA.
The minister, speaking at a one-day symposium on the disease, said the rest of the AIDS victims among Iran's 60 million people had been infected by contaminated blood.
Marandi did not say how many people in Iran were infected with HIV, the virus that causes the disease, but did not yet have full-blown AIDS.

According to United Nations figures, about 22 million people are HIV-positive or suffer from AIDS, with 3.1 million new infections in 1996. One and a half million people died from AIDS last year, the figures show.
